key_insight: Adaptive variational quantum chemistry can become trapped by the fermion-to-qubit mapping itself, with point-group symmetry preserving trainability only when the representation is also favorable.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum algorithm design, representation choice, symmetry handling, and runtime shot allocation must be co-optimized to avoid flat gradients and wasted circuit executions.
method: Tested a spin-conserved SUSD operator pool on stretched LiH, BeH2, and H2O geometries.
Compared asymmetric distortions against symmetric BeH2 to isolate representation-induced trapping effects.
Added a covariance-driven shot-allocation filter that monitors gradient precision and terminates flat-lined circuits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic evaluation at 2× equilibrium stretch across multiple molecules, showing that Bravyi-Kitaev mapping can create optimization trapping under asymmetric distortions while symmetric BeH2 remains better conditioned.
watch_item: The proposed runtime pruning and termination logic may depend on reliable gradient-noise estimates, so it could be fragile on hardware with limited measurement precision.
paper_title: Representation-Induced Symmetry Trapping in Adaptive Variational Quantum Simulations of Multi-Reference Topologies
